AgencyAcknowledgmentEmployee AcknowledgmentIntroductionAbout This Handbook This Employee Handbook is issued by Sample 1 (referred to throughout as “the Company”). It is effective Sample 2 and applies to all employees. Questions about any policy may be directed to Sample text 4
Second line 4.This handbook is designed to acquaint you with the Company and provide information about working conditions, benefits, and policies affecting your employment. You should read, understand, and comply with all provisions of the handbook. It describes many of your responsibilities as an employee and outlines the programs the Company has developed to benefit you.No handbook can anticipate every circumstance or question. As the Company continues to grow, the need may arise to revise, supplement, or rescind policies, or to adopt new ones. The Company reserves the right to do so at any time, with or without notice, except for its policy of at-will employment. This handbook is not a contract of employment and does not create contractual rights of any kind.Section 1: Governing Principles of EmploymentWelcome Statement Welcome to the Company. Whether you are beginning your employment or have been with us for some time, we are glad you are part of our team. Our employees provide the service and quality our customers rely on, and your contribution helps us grow and create new opportunities in the years ahead.Definitions The term “Company” refers to your employer. The term “employee” refers to a person employed by the Company. The term “Human Resources” refers to the Company's Human Resources function or the individual designated to perform that role.Equal Employment Opportunity The Company is an equal opportunity employer. It guarantees every applicant and employee equal treatment without regard to race (including traits historically associated with race, such as hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, transfer, training, compensation, benefits, and separation. Employees with questions or concerns about equal employment opportunity are encouraged to contact Human Resources. The Company prohibits retaliation against anyone who raises a good-faith concern under this policy.Background Checks & Fair Chance Hiring optionalThe Company may conduct background checks on applicants and employees where permitted by law and relevant to the position. Any consumer report is obtained only after separate written disclosure and authorization, as required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act.Consistent with applicable “ban the box” and fair chance laws, the Company does not ask about criminal history on the initial application and does not consider criminal history until after a conditional offer of employment has been made. A criminal record does not automatically disqualify an applicant. Where a record is considered, the Company performs an individualized assessment of the nature and gravity of the offense, the time that has passed, and the relationship of the offense to the duties of the position.If the Company intends to take adverse action based in whole or in part on a background report, the applicant or employee will receive advance notice, a copy of the report, a summary of rights, and a reasonable opportunity to respond or provide evidence of rehabilitation before a final decision is made.Disability & Religious Accommodation Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act and applicable state law, the Company will provide reasonable accommodation to a qualified employee or applicant with a known disability, unless doing so would cause undue hardship. The Company will likewise reasonably accommodate an employee's sincerely held religious beliefs or practices absent undue hardship.An employee who needs an accommodation should notify Human Resources, preferably in writing. The Company will engage in a good-faith interactive process to identify an effective accommodation. The Company makes the final determination as to which reasonable accommodation, if any, will be provided.Pregnancy, Childbirth & Related Conditions The Company provides reasonable accommodations to qualified employees and applicants for known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions, as required by the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act and applicable state law, unless doing so would impose an undue hardship.Accommodations are determined through an interactive discussion between the employee and Sample text 4
Second line 4. Examples may include additional or longer breaks, seating, closer parking, flexible scheduling, temporary reassignment or light duty, limits on lifting, remote work where the job permits, and leave when no other accommodation is effective. An employee will not be required to accept an accommodation without discussion, and will not be forced to take leave if another reasonable accommodation would allow the employee to keep working.Under the PUMP Act, the Company provides reasonable break time and a private space, other than a bathroom, that is shielded from view and free from intrusion, for an employee to express breast milk for one year after the child's birth. See also the Lactation Accommodation policy.Retaliation against any employee who requests or uses an accommodation under this policy is prohibited.Lactation Accommodation The Company provides reasonable break time and a private space, other than a restroom, for an employee to express breast milk for a nursing child, in accordance with federal and applicable state law. Employees who need this accommodation should contact Human Resources. The Company prohibits retaliation against employees who exercise their rights under this policy.At-Will Employment Employment with the Company is at-will. This means that either you or the Company may end the employment relationship at any time, for any reason or no reason, with or without cause or notice, subject to applicable law. No supervisor, manager, or representative of the Company, other than its highest-ranking officer, has authority to alter the at-will relationship or to enter into an agreement for employment for a specified period, and any such agreement must be in writing and signed. Nothing in this handbook limits either party's right to terminate the employment relationship at will.Anti-Harassment, Discrimination & Retaliation The Company is committed to a work environment free of harassment, discrimination, and retaliation. It prohibits harassment and discrimination based on any characteristic protected by law, including sexual harassment. Prohibited conduct includes unwelcome advances, requests for favors, slurs, jokes, intimidation, and other verbal, visual, or physical conduct that creates an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment.Any employee who believes they have experienced or witnessed harassment, discrimination, or retaliation should report it promptly to their supervisor or Human Resources. All complaints will be investigated promptly and as confidentially as practical, and appropriate corrective action will be taken. The Company strictly prohibits retaliation against anyone who reports a concern in good faith or participates in an investigation. Employees may also file a charge with the federal Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) or the applicable state agency.Open Door Policy The Company encourages open, honest communication. If you have a concern about your work, a policy, or a decision, you are encouraged to raise it first with your supervisor. If that is not appropriate or does not resolve the matter, you may take it to the next level of management or to Human Resources. Most concerns can be resolved by discussing them openly.Whistleblower Protection & Anti-Retaliation Employees are encouraged and expected to report, in good faith, any conduct they reasonably believe violates a law, regulation, or Company policy, including suspected fraud, theft, falsification of records, unsafe working conditions, discrimination or harassment, wage violations, or environmental violations. Reports may be made to a supervisor, to Sample text 4
Second line 4, or to any member of management.The Company prohibits retaliation of any kind against an employee who makes a good faith report, who participates in an investigation, who refuses to participate in activity the employee reasonably believes is unlawful, or who exercises any right protected by law. Retaliation includes termination, demotion, discipline, reduction in hours or pay, reassignment, threats, and exclusion.Nothing in this handbook limits an employee's right to report suspected violations directly to a government agency (including the EEOC, OSHA, the Department of Labor, the NLRB, the SEC, or a state equivalent) or to participate in an agency proceeding. Employees do not need Company permission and are not required to notify the Company first. An employee who believes retaliation has occurred should report it to Sample text 4
Second line 4 immediately; retaliation is itself a violation of this policy and is subject to discipline up to and including termination.Respect for Others The Company values healthy, respectful working relationships. Employees are expected to treat one another, and customers, with courtesy and professionalism. Disrespectful behavior (including spreading rumors, making untruthful or malicious statements about others, or similar conduct) undermines the workplace and may result in discipline, up to and including termination.Drug- and Alcohol-Free Workplace To protect the safety and productivity of all employees, the Company maintains a workplace free of illegal drugs and alcohol misuse. The unlawful use, possession, sale, or distribution of illegal drugs, and reporting to work under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs, are prohibited. Employees taking prescription or over-the-counter medication that may impair job performance or safety must notify their supervisor. Violation of this policy may result in discipline, up to and including termination, consistent with applicable law.Workplace Violence Prevention The Company is committed to a safe workplace and does not tolerate threats, threatening behavior, intimidation, or acts of violence by or against employees, customers, or visitors. Weapons are prohibited on Company premises to the extent permitted by law. Any threat or act of violence should be reported immediately to management. Reports made in good faith will not result in retaliation, and all reports will be investigated. Violations may result in discipline, up to and including termination, and referral to law enforcement.Right to Revise This handbook contains the Company's current employment policies. Except for the policy of at-will employment, the Company reserves the right to revise, modify, delete, or add to any policy, procedure, work rule, or benefit at any time, with or without notice. Written changes supersede prior policy. No oral statement can alter the provisions of this handbook.Section 2: Workplace & CompensationEmployee Classifications Each employee is classified as full-time, part-time, or temporary/seasonal, and as either exempt or non-exempt under federal and state wage-and-hour law. Non-exempt employees are entitled to overtime and any legally required meal and rest breaks; exempt employees are not eligible for overtime. Benefit eligibility depends on classification. Your classification does not change your at-will status. You will be told your classification at hire and of any later change.Introductory Period The beginning of employment is an introductory period during which you and the Company can evaluate whether the position is a good fit. The Company may extend this period at its discretion. Completing the introductory period does not change your at-will status or create any guarantee of continued employment.Job Duties Your supervisor will explain your job responsibilities and the standards expected of you. Job duties may change over time, and you may be asked to perform additional or different work as needed. The Company may alter job responsibilities, reassign positions, or add duties at any time, with or without notice.Personnel Records The Company maintains a personnel file for each employee. You are responsible for keeping your information current (including address, telephone number, emergency contact, and tax-withholding details) by notifying Human Resources of any change. Accurate records are important for pay, benefits, and reaching you in an emergency.Employment Eligibility Verification (Form I-9) Federal law requires the Company to verify the identity and employment authorization of every person hired. Each new employee must complete Section 1 of Form I-9 no later than the first day of work and present acceptable original documentation within three business days of the start date. Employees choose which acceptable documents to present; the Company does not specify or demand particular documents, and does not request more or different documents than the law requires.Where an employee's employment authorization document carries an expiration date, the Company will reverify authorization on or before the expiration date. The Company does not reverify U.S. passports, Permanent Resident Cards, or List B identity documents. Employees are asked to provide updated documentation in advance to avoid an interruption in work.The Company complies with the anti-discrimination provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act. It does not treat employees differently in hiring, verification, or reverification on the basis of citizenship status or national origin, and does not retaliate against an employee for asserting rights under those provisions.Employment References & Verification optionalAll requests for employment verification or references (from lenders, prospective employers, background screening firms, or government agencies) must be directed to Sample text 4
Second line 4. Supervisors and coworkers should not respond to reference requests on the Company's behalf.Unless the employee provides written authorization to release more, the Company confirms only dates of employment, position(s) held, and, where required by law or requested for verification of income, rate of pay. This practice protects both the employee and the Company and ensures that information released is accurate and consistent.Work Schedules, Meal & Rest Breaks You will be assigned a work schedule and are expected to begin and end work accordingly. Business needs may require schedule changes. Non-exempt employees must take any meal and rest breaks required by applicable state law; specific requirements are described in the State-Specific Supplement to this handbook. Employees must be fully relieved of duty during unpaid meal periods. If you are ever unable to take a required break, notify your supervisor or Human Resources promptly.Timekeeping Non-exempt employees must accurately record all time worked, including the start and end of each shift and of any unpaid meal period, using the Company's timekeeping system. Working “off the clock” is prohibited, and no supervisor may ask you to do so. Falsifying or altering time records is prohibited and may result in discipline, up to and including termination. Report any timekeeping error to your supervisor right away.Overtime Non-exempt employees are paid overtime as required by federal and applicable state law, generally one-and-one-half times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek. Some states also require daily overtime; where that applies, it is described in the State-Specific Supplement. Overtime must be authorized in advance by management. Unauthorized overtime will be paid but may result in discipline.Meal & Rest Periods Non-exempt employees are provided meal and rest periods in accordance with federal and state law. Where state law requires them, meal periods are generally at least thirty minutes and rest periods at least ten minutes for every four hours worked or major fraction thereof. Specific requirements for your work location appear in the State-Specific Supplement.Meal periods are unpaid and duty-free. An employee must be fully relieved of all duties and free to leave the work area. An employee who is interrupted, asked to remain on duty, or unable to take a full meal period must report this to a supervisor the same day so the time is paid correctly. Rest periods are paid and count as time worked; they may not be combined with a meal period, used to arrive late or leave early, or accumulated.Working through a meal or rest period without authorization is not permitted. An employee who does so will be paid for the time and may be subject to discipline for failing to follow this policy.Paychecks & Deductions You will be paid on the Company's regular payroll schedule. Your pay statement itemizes gross earnings and all deductions, including legally required taxes and withholdings. The Company complies with federal and state law regarding wage deductions. If you believe there is an error in your pay, report it to Human Resources or payroll immediately so it can be corrected; the Company prohibits retaliation for raising a good-faith pay concern.Pay Transparency & Wage Discussions Employees have the right to inquire about, discuss, and disclose their own wages and the wages of other employees. The Company will not discharge, discipline, or otherwise retaliate against an employee for doing so, and no policy, agreement, or instruction from a supervisor may be interpreted to prohibit such discussions. Employees whose regular job duties give them access to compensation information may not disclose that information without authorization, except as permitted by law.Where required by state or local law, the Company discloses the pay scale or wage range for a position in the job posting, on request from an applicant, and on request from a current employee for the employee's own position. The Company does not ask applicants about salary history where that inquiry is prohibited by law, and does not rely on salary history to set pay.Pay decisions are based on job-related factors including experience, skill, education, certifications, performance, geography, and market data. Any employee who believes a pay decision was made on a basis prohibited by law should raise it with Sample text 4
Second line 4.Payroll Errors & Improper Deduction Safe Harbor optionalThe Company intends to pay every employee accurately and on time, and to comply with the salary basis requirements for exempt employees. Improper deductions from an exempt employee's salary are prohibited.An employee who believes a paycheck is incorrect (whether an underpayment, an overpayment, an unauthorized deduction, or missing hours) should report it to Sample text 4
Second line 4 immediately. The Company will investigate promptly, and any improper deduction or underpayment confirmed will be reimbursed on the next regular payroll or sooner where required by law. An employee will not be retaliated against for reporting a suspected payroll error.Where an overpayment has occurred, the Company will notify the employee, explain the amount and cause, and arrange repayment on terms consistent with applicable law. Deductions to recover an overpayment are made only with the employee's written authorization where such authorization is required.Wage Garnishments & Support Orders optionalThe Company is required by law to honor valid garnishment orders, child support withholding orders, tax levies, and similar legal process. When such an order is received, the Company will notify the affected employee, provide a copy of the order where permitted, and begin withholding on the schedule the order requires.The Company withholds only the amount the order and applicable law allow, applies the limits of the Consumer Credit Protection Act and any stricter state limit, and will not disclose the existence of an order to coworkers. An employee will not be discharged because wages are garnished for any one indebtedness. Questions about the underlying debt must be directed to the issuing court or agency; the Company cannot modify, delay, or contest the order on an employee's behalf.Expense Reimbursement The Company reimburses employees for reasonable, necessary, and pre-approved business expenses incurred in performing their jobs, consistent with applicable law and Company procedure. Submit required receipts and an expense form promptly. Employees should obtain approval before incurring a significant business expense, and should contact their supervisor with any questions about reimbursement.Attendance & Punctuality optionalRegular attendance and punctuality are essential. If you will be late or absent, notify your supervisor as early as possible in accordance with Company call-in procedures. Excessive absenteeism or tardiness, or failure to notify the Company, may result in discipline, up to and including termination. Absences protected by law will be handled in accordance with the applicable leave policy.Section 3: Benefits & Time OffBenefits Overview The Company offers a range of benefits to eligible employees. This handbook summarizes them in general terms only. The specific terms, eligibility, and conditions of each benefit plan are governed by the official plan documents and insurance contracts, which control in the event of any difference with this handbook. The Company may change, add, or discontinue benefits at any time consistent with applicable law and plan terms.When You Can Enroll optionalThere are three times you can enroll in or change your benefits.When you are first eligible. New employees may enroll during the initial enrollment window described in your offer or benefits summary. If you do not enroll during that window, you must wait for open enrollment unless you have a qualifying life event.Open enrollment. Once a year the Company holds an open enrollment period. This is the one time you can add, drop or change coverage for any reason. Elections made during open enrollment take effect on the first day of the new plan year and generally cannot be changed until the following year.A qualifying life event. Certain life changes let you change coverage mid-year, see the next section. You generally have 30 days from the event to make the change, and the Company may require documentation.If you take no action during open enrollment, your current elections may carry forward or may default to no coverage, depending on the plan. Read the enrollment materials each year; do not assume.Health & Insurance Benefits Eligible employees may participate in the Company's health and related insurance benefits, subject to the terms of the applicable plans. Human Resources can provide summary plan descriptions and enrollment information. Continuation of coverage after certain qualifying events may be available under COBRA or applicable state continuation law.Understanding Your Benefits: Plain English optionalBenefits paperwork is full of terms that are rarely explained. Here is what they actually mean.Premium, what the coverage costs each pay period, whether or not you use it. Your share is deducted from your paycheck.Deductible, what you pay out of pocket each plan year before the plan starts paying its share. A $2,000 deductible means the first $2,000 of covered care is yours.Copay, a flat amount for a specific service, such as $30 to see a doctor. Copays often apply before you meet the deductible.Coinsurance (after the deductible, the percentage you keep paying. “80/20” means the plan pays 80% and you pay 20%.Out-of-pocket maximum) the most you can pay in a plan year. Once you reach it, the plan pays 100% of covered in-network care. This is the number that protects you from a catastrophe.In-network, providers who agreed to discounted rates. Going out of network costs dramatically more, and sometimes is not covered at all. Check before you book.HSA and FSA, accounts that let you pay medical costs with pre-tax dollars. An HSA requires a high-deductible plan, the money is yours permanently and it rolls over. An FSA does not require a specific plan, but is largely use-it-or-lose-it within the plan year.Continuation of Health Coverage (COBRA) optionalWhen Company-sponsored group health coverage would otherwise end because of a qualifying event, an employee and covered dependents may have the right to continue that coverage for a limited period at their own expense under COBRA or a comparable state continuation law.Qualifying events include termination of employment for reasons other than gross misconduct, a reduction in hours below the eligibility threshold, divorce or legal separation, a dependent child aging out of the plan, and the death of the employee. The Company will provide an election notice through the plan administrator following a qualifying event. The employee or dependent is responsible for notifying Sample text 4

Nada en este manual limita el derecho de cualquiera de las partes a terminar la relación laboral a voluntad.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "harassment", "group": "Section 1: Governing Principles of Employment", "title_en": "Anti-Harassment, Discrimination & Retaliation", "title_es": "Contra el Acoso, la Discriminación y las Represalias", "body_en": "<p>The Company is committed to a work environment free of harassment, discrimination, and retaliation. It prohibits harassment and discrimination based on any characteristic protected by law, including sexual harassment. Prohibited conduct includes unwelcome advances, requests for favors, slurs, jokes, intimidation, and other verbal, visual, or physical conduct that creates an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment.</p><p>Any employee who believes they have experienced or witnessed harassment, discrimination, or retaliation should report it promptly to their supervisor or Human Resources. All complaints will be investigated promptly and as confidentially as practical, and appropriate corrective action will be taken. The Company strictly prohibits retaliation against anyone who reports a concern in good faith or participates in an investigation. Employees may also file a charge with the federal Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) or the applicable state agency.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía está comprometida con un entorno de trabajo libre de acoso, discriminación y represalias. Prohíbe el acoso y la discriminación basados en cualquier característica protegida por la ley, incluido el acoso sexual. La conducta prohibida incluye insinuaciones no deseadas, solicitudes de favores, insultos, bromas, intimidación y otra conducta verbal, visual o física que cree un entorno de trabajo intimidante, hostil u ofensivo.</p><p>Todo empleado que crea haber sufrido o presenciado acoso, discriminación o represalias debe informarlo de inmediato a su supervisor o a Recursos Humanos. Todas las quejas se investigarán con prontitud y de la manera más confidencial posible, y se tomarán las medidas correctivas apropiadas. La Compañía prohíbe estrictamente las represalias contra quien informe una inquietud de buena fe o participe en una investigación. Los empleados también pueden presentar un cargo ante la Comisión Federal para la Igualdad de Oportunidades en el Empleo (EEOC) o la agencia estatal correspondiente.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "opendoor", "group": "Section 1: Governing Principles of Employment", "title_en": "Open Door Policy", "title_es": "Política de Puertas Abiertas", "body_en": "<p>The Company encourages open, honest communication. If you have a concern about your work, a policy, or a decision, you are encouraged to raise it first with your supervisor. If that is not appropriate or does not resolve the matter, you may take it to the next level of management or to Human Resources. Most concerns can be resolved by discussing them openly.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía fomenta una comunicación abierta y honesta. Si tiene una inquietud sobre su trabajo, una política o una decisión, se le anima a plantearla primero con su supervisor. Si eso no es apropiado o no resuelve el asunto, puede llevarlo al siguiente nivel de gerencia o a Recursos Humanos. La mayoría de las inquietudes pueden resolverse discutiéndolas abiertamente.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "whistleblower", "group": "Section 1: Governing Principles of Employment", "title_en": "Whistleblower Protection & Anti-Retaliation", "title_es": "Protección al Denunciante y Prohibición de Represalias", "body_en": "<p>Employees are encouraged and expected to report, in good faith, any conduct they reasonably believe violates a law, regulation, or Company policy, including suspected fraud, theft, falsification of records, unsafe working conditions, discrimination or harassment, wage violations, or environmental violations. Reports may be made to a supervisor, to {{HR_CONTACT}}, or to any member of management.</p><p>The Company prohibits retaliation of any kind against an employee who makes a good faith report, who participates in an investigation, who refuses to participate in activity the employee reasonably believes is unlawful, or who exercises any right protected by law. Retaliation includes termination, demotion, discipline, reduction in hours or pay, reassignment, threats, and exclusion.</p><p>Nothing in this handbook limits an employee's right to report suspected violations directly to a government agency (including the EEOC, OSHA, the Department of Labor, the NLRB, the SEC, or a state equivalent) or to participate in an agency proceeding. Employees do not need Company permission and are not required to notify the Company first. An employee who believes retaliation has occurred should report it to {{HR_CONTACT}} immediately; retaliation is itself a violation of this policy and is subject to discipline up to and including termination.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Se anima y se espera que los empleados denuncien, de buena fe, cualquier conducta que razonablemente consideren que infringe una ley, un reglamento o una política de la Compañía, incluidos presuntos fraudes, robos, falsificación de registros, condiciones de trabajo inseguras, discriminación u hostigamiento, infracciones salariales o infracciones ambientales. Las denuncias pueden hacerse a un supervisor, a {{HR_CONTACT}} o a cualquier miembro de la gerencia.</p><p>La Compañía prohíbe todo tipo de represalia contra un empleado que presente una denuncia de buena fe, que participe en una investigación, que se niegue a participar en una actividad que razonablemente considere ilegal, o que ejerza cualquier derecho protegido por ley. Las represalias incluyen despido, degradación, medidas disciplinarias, reducción de horas o de salario, reasignación, amenazas y exclusión.</p><p>Nada en este manual limita el derecho de un empleado a denunciar presuntas infracciones directamente ante una agencia gubernamental (incluidas la EEOC, OSHA, el Departamento de Trabajo, la NLRB, la SEC o su equivalente estatal) ni a participar en un procedimiento de una agencia. Los empleados no necesitan permiso de la Compañía ni están obligados a notificarle primero. Todo empleado que considere que ha sufrido represalias debe informarlo de inmediato a {{HR_CONTACT}}; la represalia constituye en sí misma una violación de esta política y está sujeta a medidas disciplinarias que pueden incluir el despido.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "respect", "group": "Section 1: Governing Principles of Employment", "title_en": "Respect for Others", "title_es": "Respeto hacia los Demás", "body_en": "<p>The Company values healthy, respectful working relationships. Employees are expected to treat one another, and customers, with courtesy and professionalism. Disrespectful behavior (including spreading rumors, making untruthful or malicious statements about others, or similar conduct) undermines the workplace and may result in discipline, up to and including termination.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía valora las relaciones laborales sanas y respetuosas. Se espera que los empleados se traten entre sí, y a los clientes, con cortesía y profesionalismo. El comportamiento irrespetuoso (incluidos la difusión de rumores, hacer declaraciones falsas o malintencionadas sobre otros, o conductas similares) socava el lugar de trabajo y puede dar lugar a medidas disciplinarias, hasta e incluyendo el despido.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "drugfree", "group": "Section 1: Governing Principles of Employment", "title_en": "Drug- and Alcohol-Free Workplace", "title_es": "Lugar de Trabajo Libre de Drogas y Alcohol", "body_en": "<p>To protect the safety and productivity of all employees, the Company maintains a workplace free of illegal drugs and alcohol misuse. The unlawful use, possession, sale, or distribution of illegal drugs, and reporting to work under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs, are prohibited. Employees taking prescription or over-the-counter medication that may impair job performance or safety must notify their supervisor. Violation of this policy may result in discipline, up to and including termination, consistent with applicable law.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Para proteger la seguridad y la productividad de todos los empleados, la Compañía mantiene un lugar de trabajo libre de drogas ilegales y del abuso del alcohol. Se prohíben el uso, la posesión, la venta o la distribución ilegales de drogas ilegales, así como presentarse a trabajar bajo la influencia del alcohol o de drogas ilegales. Los empleados que tomen medicamentos con receta o de venta libre que puedan afectar el desempeño laboral o la seguridad deben notificar a su supervisor. La violación de esta política puede dar lugar a medidas disciplinarias, hasta e incluyendo el despido, de conformidad con la ley aplicable.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "violence", "group": "Section 1: Governing Principles of Employment", "title_en": "Workplace Violence Prevention", "title_es": "Prevención de la Violencia en el Trabajo", "body_en": "<p>The Company is committed to a safe workplace and does not tolerate threats, threatening behavior, intimidation, or acts of violence by or against employees, customers, or visitors. Weapons are prohibited on Company premises to the extent permitted by law. Any threat or act of violence should be reported immediately to management. Reports made in good faith will not result in retaliation, and all reports will be investigated. Violations may result in discipline, up to and including termination, and referral to law enforcement.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía está comprometida con un lugar de trabajo seguro y no tolera amenazas, comportamientos amenazantes, intimidación ni actos de violencia por parte de o contra empleados, clientes o visitantes. Se prohíben las armas en las instalaciones de la Compañía en la medida permitida por la ley. Toda amenaza o acto de violencia debe informarse de inmediato a la gerencia. Los informes hechos de buena fe no darán lugar a represalias, y todos los informes serán investigados. Las violaciones pueden dar lugar a medidas disciplinarias, hasta e incluyendo el despido, y a la remisión a las autoridades.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "revise", "group": "Section 1: Governing Principles of Employment", "title_en": "Right to Revise", "title_es": "Derecho a Revisar", "body_en": "<p>This handbook contains the Company's current employment policies. Except for the policy of at-will employment, the Company reserves the right to revise, modify, delete, or add to any policy, procedure, work rule, or benefit at any time, with or without notice. Written changes supersede prior policy. No oral statement can alter the provisions of this handbook.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Este manual contiene las políticas de empleo vigentes de la Compañía. Salvo la política de empleo a voluntad, la Compañía se reserva el derecho de revisar, modificar, eliminar o agregar cualquier política, procedimiento, regla de trabajo o beneficio en cualquier momento, con o sin previo aviso. Los cambios por escrito sustituyen las políticas anteriores. Ninguna declaración verbal puede alterar las disposiciones de este manual.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "dei", "group": "Section 1: Governing Principles of Employment", "title_en": "Diversity, Equity & Inclusion", "title_es": "Diversidad, Equidad e Inclusión", "body_en": "<p>The Company is committed to a workplace that is diverse, equitable, and inclusive, where every employee is treated with dignity and respect. We value the range of backgrounds and perspectives our employees bring and strive to provide access, opportunity, and advancement for all. Conduct inconsistent with these values may result in discipline.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía está comprometida con un lugar de trabajo diverso, equitativo e inclusivo, donde cada empleado sea tratado con dignidad y respeto. Valoramos la diversidad de orígenes y perspectivas que aportan nuestros empleados y nos esforzamos por brindar acceso, oportunidad y avance para todos. La conducta incompatible con estos valores puede dar lugar a medidas disciplinarias.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "classifications", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Employee Classifications", "title_es": "Clasificaciones de Empleados", "body_en": "<p>Each employee is classified as full-time, part-time, or temporary/seasonal, and as either exempt or non-exempt under federal and state wage-and-hour law. Non-exempt employees are entitled to overtime and any legally required meal and rest breaks; exempt employees are not eligible for overtime. Benefit eligibility depends on classification. Your classification does not change your at-will status. You will be told your classification at hire and of any later change.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Cada empleado se clasifica como de tiempo completo, de tiempo parcial o temporal/de temporada, y como exento o no exento según la ley federal y estatal de salarios y horas. Los empleados no exentos tienen derecho a horas extra y a los períodos de comida y descanso exigidos por la ley; los empleados exentos no son elegibles para horas extra. La elegibilidad para beneficios depende de la clasificación. Su clasificación no cambia su condición de empleo a voluntad. Se le informará su clasificación al momento de la contratación y de cualquier cambio posterior.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "introperiod", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Introductory Period", "title_es": "Período de Introducción", "body_en": "<p>The beginning of employment is an introductory period during which you and the Company can evaluate whether the position is a good fit. The Company may extend this period at its discretion. Completing the introductory period does not change your at-will status or create any guarantee of continued employment.</p>", "body_es": "<p>El inicio del empleo es un período de introducción durante el cual usted y la Compañía pueden evaluar si el puesto es adecuado. La Compañía puede extender este período a su discreción. Completar el período de introducción no cambia su condición de empleo a voluntad ni crea garantía alguna de empleo continuo.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "jobduties", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Job Duties", "title_es": "Deberes del Puesto", "body_en": "<p>Your supervisor will explain your job responsibilities and the standards expected of you. Job duties may change over time, and you may be asked to perform additional or different work as needed. The Company may alter job responsibilities, reassign positions, or add duties at any time, with or without notice.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Su supervisor le explicará sus responsabilidades laborales y los estándares que se esperan de usted. Los deberes del puesto pueden cambiar con el tiempo, y se le puede pedir que realice trabajo adicional o diferente según sea necesario. La Compañía puede modificar las responsabilidades laborales, reasignar puestos o agregar deberes en cualquier momento, con o sin previo aviso.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "records", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Personnel Records", "title_es": "Expedientes de Personal", "body_en": "<p>The Company maintains a personnel file for each employee. You are responsible for keeping your information current (including address, telephone number, emergency contact, and tax-withholding details) by notifying Human Resources of any change. Accurate records are important for pay, benefits, and reaching you in an emergency.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía mantiene un expediente de personal para cada empleado. Usted es responsable de mantener su información actualizada (incluidos su dirección, número de teléfono, contacto de emergencia y datos de retención de impuestos) notificando a Recursos Humanos cualquier cambio. Los registros precisos son importantes para el pago, los beneficios y para localizarlo en caso de emergencia.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "i9", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Employment Eligibility Verification (Form I-9)", "title_es": "Verificación de Elegibilidad de Empleo (Formulario I-9)", "body_en": "<p>Federal law requires the Company to verify the identity and employment authorization of every person hired. Each new employee must complete Section 1 of Form I-9 no later than the first day of work and present acceptable original documentation within three business days of the start date. Employees choose which acceptable documents to present; the Company does not specify or demand particular documents, and does not request more or different documents than the law requires.</p><p>Where an employee's employment authorization document carries an expiration date, the Company will reverify authorization on or before the expiration date. The Company does not reverify U.S. passports, Permanent Resident Cards, or List B identity documents. Employees are asked to provide updated documentation in advance to avoid an interruption in work.</p><p>The Company complies with the anti-discrimination provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act. It does not treat employees differently in hiring, verification, or reverification on the basis of citizenship status or national origin, and does not retaliate against an employee for asserting rights under those provisions.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La ley federal exige que la Compañía verifique la identidad y la autorización de empleo de toda persona contratada. Cada empleado nuevo debe completar la Sección 1 del Formulario I-9 a más tardar el primer día de trabajo y presentar documentación original aceptable dentro de los tres días hábiles siguientes a la fecha de inicio. Los empleados eligen qué documentos aceptables presentar; la Compañía no especifica ni exige documentos concretos, ni solicita más documentos o documentos distintos de los que la ley requiere.</p><p>Cuando el documento de autorización de empleo de un empleado tenga fecha de vencimiento, la Compañía volverá a verificar la autorización en la fecha de vencimiento o antes. La Compañía no vuelve a verificar pasaportes estadounidenses, Tarjetas de Residente Permanente ni documentos de identidad de la Lista B. Se solicita a los empleados que presenten documentación actualizada con anticipación para evitar una interrupción del trabajo.</p><p>La Compañía cumple con las disposiciones antidiscriminatorias de la Ley de Inmigración y Nacionalidad. No trata de manera diferente a los empleados en la contratación, la verificación o la reverificación por motivos de estatus de ciudadanía u origen nacional, ni toma represalias contra un empleado por hacer valer sus derechos conforme a dichas disposiciones.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "references", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Employment References & Verification", "title_es": "Referencias y Verificación de Empleo", "body_en": "<p>All requests for employment verification or references (from lenders, prospective employers, background screening firms, or government agencies) must be directed to {{HR_CONTACT}}. Supervisors and coworkers should not respond to reference requests on the Company's behalf.</p><p>Unless the employee provides written authorization to release more, the Company confirms only dates of employment, position(s) held, and, where required by law or requested for verification of income, rate of pay. This practice protects both the employee and the Company and ensures that information released is accurate and consistent.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Todas las solicitudes de verificación de empleo o de referencias (de prestamistas, empleadores potenciales, empresas de verificación de antecedentes o agencias gubernamentales) deben dirigirse a {{HR_CONTACT}}. Los supervisores y compañeros de trabajo no deben responder solicitudes de referencia en nombre de la Compañía.</p><p>Salvo que el empleado otorgue autorización por escrito para divulgar más información, la Compañía confirma únicamente las fechas de empleo, el o los puestos ocupados y, cuando la ley lo exija o se solicite para verificar ingresos, la tasa de pago. Esta práctica protege tanto al empleado como a la Compañía y garantiza que la información divulgada sea exacta y coherente.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "schedules", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Work Schedules, Meal & Rest Breaks", "title_es": "Horarios de Trabajo, Comidas y Descansos", "body_en": "<p>You will be assigned a work schedule and are expected to begin and end work accordingly. Business needs may require schedule changes. Non-exempt employees must take any meal and rest breaks required by applicable state law; specific requirements are described in the State-Specific Supplement to this handbook. Employees must be fully relieved of duty during unpaid meal periods. If you are ever unable to take a required break, notify your supervisor or Human Resources promptly.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Se le asignará un horario de trabajo y se espera que comience y termine su labor de acuerdo con él. Las necesidades del negocio pueden requerir cambios de horario. Los empleados no exentos deben tomar los períodos de comida y descanso exigidos por la ley estatal aplicable; los requisitos específicos se describen en el Suplemento Específico del Estado de este manual. Los empleados deben quedar totalmente relevados de sus funciones durante los períodos de comida no pagados. Si alguna vez no puede tomar un descanso requerido, notifique a su supervisor o a Recursos Humanos de inmediato.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "timekeeping", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Timekeeping", "title_es": "Registro de Horas", "body_en": "<p>Non-exempt employees must accurately record all time worked, including the start and end of each shift and of any unpaid meal period, using the Company's timekeeping system. Working “off the clock” is prohibited, and no supervisor may ask you to do so. Falsifying or altering time records is prohibited and may result in discipline, up to and including termination. Report any timekeeping error to your supervisor right away.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Los empleados no exentos deben registrar con exactitud todo el tiempo trabajado, incluidos el inicio y el fin de cada turno y de cualquier período de comida no pagado, utilizando el sistema de registro de horas de la Compañía. Está prohibido trabajar “fuera de horario”, y ningún supervisor puede pedirle que lo haga. Falsificar o alterar los registros de horas está prohibido y puede dar lugar a medidas disciplinarias, hasta e incluyendo el despido. Informe cualquier error de registro a su supervisor de inmediato.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "overtime", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Overtime", "title_es": "Horas Extra", "body_en": "<p>Non-exempt employees are paid overtime as required by federal and applicable state law, generally one-and-one-half times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek. Some states also require daily overtime; where that applies, it is described in the State-Specific Supplement. Overtime must be authorized in advance by management. Unauthorized overtime will be paid but may result in discipline.</p>", "body_es": "<p>A los empleados no exentos se les pagan horas extra según lo exigido por la ley federal y estatal aplicable, generalmente una vez y media la tarifa regular por las horas trabajadas por encima de 40 en una semana laboral. Algunos estados también exigen horas extra diarias; cuando corresponda, se describe en el Suplemento Específico del Estado. Las horas extra deben ser autorizadas con anticipación por la gerencia. Las horas extra no autorizadas se pagarán, pero pueden dar lugar a medidas disciplinarias.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "mealrest", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Meal & Rest Periods", "title_es": "Períodos de Comida y Descanso", "body_en": "<p>Non-exempt employees are provided meal and rest periods in accordance with federal and state law. Where state law requires them, meal periods are generally at least thirty minutes and rest periods at least ten minutes for every four hours worked or major fraction thereof. Specific requirements for your work location appear in the State-Specific Supplement.</p><p>Meal periods are unpaid and duty-free. An employee must be fully relieved of all duties and free to leave the work area. An employee who is interrupted, asked to remain on duty, or unable to take a full meal period must report this to a supervisor the same day so the time is paid correctly. Rest periods are paid and count as time worked; they may not be combined with a meal period, used to arrive late or leave early, or accumulated.</p><p>Working through a meal or rest period without authorization is not permitted. An employee who does so will be paid for the time and may be subject to discipline for failing to follow this policy.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Los empleados no exentos reciben períodos de comida y descanso conforme a la ley federal y estatal. Cuando la ley estatal lo exige, los períodos de comida son generalmente de al menos treinta minutos y los períodos de descanso de al menos diez minutos por cada cuatro horas trabajadas o fracción mayor de las mismas. Los requisitos específicos de su lugar de trabajo aparecen en el Suplemento Específico del Estado.</p><p>Los períodos de comida no son remunerados y están libres de funciones. El empleado debe quedar totalmente relevado de todas sus obligaciones y libre de salir del área de trabajo. El empleado que sea interrumpido, a quien se le pida permanecer de servicio o que no pueda tomar un período de comida completo debe informarlo a un supervisor el mismo día para que el tiempo se pague correctamente. Los períodos de descanso son remunerados y cuentan como tiempo trabajado; no pueden combinarse con un período de comida, usarse para llegar tarde o salir temprano, ni acumularse.</p><p>No se permite trabajar durante un período de comida o descanso sin autorización. Al empleado que lo haga se le pagará el tiempo y podrá estar sujeto a medidas disciplinarias por no seguir esta política.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "traveltime", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Travel Time & On-Call Pay", "title_es": "Tiempo de Viaje y Pago por Disponibilidad", "body_en": "<p>Ordinary commuting between home and the regular worksite is not compensable. For non-exempt employees, the Company pays for travel time as follows: travel between job sites during the workday is paid; travel to a temporary or distant worksite in excess of the normal commute is paid; and travel that keeps an employee away from home overnight is paid for the hours that fall within the employee's normal working hours, on any day of the week.</p><p>An employee who is required to remain on-call and whose freedom of movement is meaningfully restricted (for example, required to remain on premises or to respond within a short window) is paid for that time. An employee who is simply reachable by phone and free to use the time for personal purposes is paid only for time actually spent working, including any minimum call-back pay required by state law.</p><p>All travel and on-call time must be recorded on the employee's timesheet. Questions about whether particular time is compensable should be raised with {{HR_CONTACT}} before the travel occurs.</p>", "body_es": "<p>El traslado ordinario entre el domicilio y el lugar de trabajo habitual no es remunerable. Para los empleados no exentos, la Compañía paga el tiempo de viaje de la siguiente manera: el viaje entre lugares de trabajo durante la jornada laboral es remunerado; el viaje a un lugar de trabajo temporal o distante que exceda el trayecto normal es remunerado; y el viaje que obliga al empleado a pernoctar fuera de casa se paga por las horas que caen dentro del horario laboral normal del empleado, cualquier día de la semana.</p><p>El empleado que deba permanecer disponible y cuya libertad de movimiento esté restringida de manera significativa (por ejemplo, que deba permanecer en las instalaciones o responder en un plazo breve) recibe pago por ese tiempo. El empleado que simplemente esté localizable por teléfono y libre de usar el tiempo para fines personales recibe pago únicamente por el tiempo efectivamente trabajado, incluido cualquier pago mínimo por llamada de regreso que exija la ley estatal.</p><p>Todo el tiempo de viaje y de disponibilidad debe registrarse en la hoja de horas del empleado. Las dudas sobre si determinado tiempo es remunerable deben plantearse a {{HR_CONTACT}} antes de que ocurra el viaje.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "paycheck", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Paychecks & Deductions", "title_es": "Checks de Pago y Deducciones", "body_en": "<p>You will be paid on the Company's regular payroll schedule. Your pay statement itemizes gross earnings and all deductions, including legally required taxes and withholdings. The Company complies with federal and state law regarding wage deductions. If you believe there is an error in your pay, report it to Human Resources or payroll immediately so it can be corrected; the Company prohibits retaliation for raising a good-faith pay concern.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Se le pagará según el calendario de nómina regular de la Compañía. Su comprobante de pago detalla las ganancias brutas y todas las deducciones, incluidos los impuestos y las retenciones exigidos por la ley. La Compañía cumple con la ley federal y estatal respecto a las deducciones salariales. Si cree que hay un error en su pago, informe a Recursos Humanos o a nómina de inmediato para que pueda corregirse; la Compañía prohíbe las represalias por plantear una inquietud salarial de buena fe.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "paytransparency", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Pay Transparency & Wage Discussions", "title_es": "Transparencia Salarial y Conversaciones sobre Salarios", "body_en": "<p>Employees have the right to inquire about, discuss, and disclose their own wages and the wages of other employees. The Company will not discharge, discipline, or otherwise retaliate against an employee for doing so, and no policy, agreement, or instruction from a supervisor may be interpreted to prohibit such discussions. Employees whose regular job duties give them access to compensation information may not disclose that information without authorization, except as permitted by law.</p><p>Where required by state or local law, the Company discloses the pay scale or wage range for a position in the job posting, on request from an applicant, and on request from a current employee for the employee's own position. The Company does not ask applicants about salary history where that inquiry is prohibited by law, and does not rely on salary history to set pay.</p><p>Pay decisions are based on job-related factors including experience, skill, education, certifications, performance, geography, and market data. Any employee who believes a pay decision was made on a basis prohibited by law should raise it with {{HR_CONTACT}}.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Los empleados tienen derecho a preguntar, comentar y divulgar su propio salario y el salario de otros empleados. La Compañía no despedirá, disciplinará ni tomará represalias de otro modo contra un empleado por hacerlo, y ninguna política, acuerdo o instrucción de un supervisor puede interpretarse en el sentido de prohibir tales conversaciones. Los empleados cuyas funciones habituales les den acceso a información de compensación no pueden divulgar dicha información sin autorización, salvo que la ley lo permita.</p><p>Cuando la ley estatal o local lo exige, la Compañía divulga la escala salarial o el rango de salario de un puesto en la publicación de la vacante, a solicitud de un solicitante y a solicitud de un empleado actual respecto de su propio puesto. La Compañía no pregunta a los solicitantes sobre su historial salarial donde dicha pregunta esté prohibida por ley, ni se basa en el historial salarial para fijar la remuneración.</p><p>Las decisiones salariales se basan en factores relacionados con el puesto, incluidos experiencia, habilidad, educación, certificaciones, desempeño, ubicación geográfica y datos de mercado. Todo empleado que considere que una decisión salarial se tomó por un motivo prohibido por la ley debe plantearlo a {{HR_CONTACT}}.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "payroll_safeharbor", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Payroll Errors & Improper Deduction Safe Harbor", "title_es": "Errores de Nómina y Salvaguarda contra Deducciones Indebidas", "body_en": "<p>The Company intends to pay every employee accurately and on time, and to comply with the salary basis requirements for exempt employees. Improper deductions from an exempt employee's salary are prohibited.</p><p>An employee who believes a paycheck is incorrect (whether an underpayment, an overpayment, an unauthorized deduction, or missing hours) should report it to {{HR_CONTACT}} immediately. The Company will investigate promptly, and any improper deduction or underpayment confirmed will be reimbursed on the next regular payroll or sooner where required by law. An employee will not be retaliated against for reporting a suspected payroll error.</p><p>Where an overpayment has occurred, the Company will notify the employee, explain the amount and cause, and arrange repayment on terms consistent with applicable law. Deductions to recover an overpayment are made only with the employee's written authorization where such authorization is required.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía tiene la intención de pagar a cada empleado de forma exacta y puntual, y de cumplir con los requisitos de pago por salario fijo para los empleados exentos. Se prohíben las deducciones indebidas del salario de un empleado exento.</p><p>El empleado que considere que su check de pago es incorrecto (ya sea por pago insuficiente, pago en exceso, una deducción no autorizada u horas faltantes) debe informarlo de inmediato a {{HR_CONTACT}}. La Compañía investigará con prontitud, y toda deducción indebida o pago insuficiente que se confirme será reembolsado en la siguiente nómina regular o antes cuando la ley lo exija. No se tomarán represalias contra un empleado por informar un presunto error de nómina.</p><p>Cuando se haya producido un pago en exceso, la Compañía notificará al empleado, explicará el monto y la causa, y acordará el reembolso en términos compatibles con la ley aplicable. Las deducciones para recuperar un pago en exceso se realizan únicamente con la autorización escrita del empleado cuando dicha autorización sea necesaria.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "directdeposit", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Direct Deposit", "title_es": "Depósito Directo", "body_en": "<p>Employees are encouraged to use direct deposit. Authorization forms are available from Human Resources. Where required by state law, direct deposit is offered as an option rather than a condition of employment.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Se anima a los empleados a utilizar el depósito directo. Los formularios de autorización están disponibles en Recursos Humanos. Cuando lo exige la ley estatal, el depósito directo se ofrece como una opción y no como una condición de empleo.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "garnishment", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Wage Garnishments & Support Orders", "title_es": "Embargos de Salario y Órdenes de Manutención", "body_en": "<p>The Company is required by law to honor valid garnishment orders, child support withholding orders, tax levies, and similar legal process. When such an order is received, the Company will notify the affected employee, provide a copy of the order where permitted, and begin withholding on the schedule the order requires.</p><p>The Company withholds only the amount the order and applicable law allow, applies the limits of the Consumer Credit Protection Act and any stricter state limit, and will not disclose the existence of an order to coworkers. An employee will not be discharged because wages are garnished for any one indebtedness. Questions about the underlying debt must be directed to the issuing court or agency; the Company cannot modify, delay, or contest the order on an employee's behalf.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La ley exige que la Compañía cumpla con las órdenes válidas de embargo de salario, las órdenes de retención por manutención de menores, los gravámenes fiscales y procesos legales similares. Cuando se recibe una orden de este tipo, la Compañía notificará al empleado afectado, le entregará una copia de la orden cuando esté permitido, y comenzará a retener según el calendario que la orden exija.</p><p>La Compañía retiene únicamente el monto que la orden y la ley aplicable permitan, aplica los límites de la Ley de Protección del Crédito al Consumidor y cualquier límite estatal más estricto, y no divulgará la existencia de una orden a los compañeros de trabajo. Ningún empleado será despedido por el embargo de su salario derivado de una sola deuda. Las preguntas sobre la deuda subyacente deben dirigirse al tribunal o agencia emisora; la Compañía no puede modificar, retrasar ni impugnar la orden en nombre del empleado.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "expenses", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Expense Reimbursement", "title_es": "Reembolso de Gastos", "body_en": "<p>The Company reimburses employees for reasonable, necessary, and pre-approved business expenses incurred in performing their jobs, consistent with applicable law and Company procedure. Submit required receipts and an expense form promptly. Employees should obtain approval before incurring a significant business expense, and should contact their supervisor with any questions about reimbursement.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía reembolsa a los empleados los gastos comerciales razonables, necesarios y aprobados previamente en que incurran al realizar su trabajo, de conformidad con la ley aplicable y el procedimiento de la Compañía. Presente los recibos requeridos y un formulario de gastos con prontitud. Los empleados deben obtener aprobación antes de incurrir en un gasto comercial significativo y deben comunicarse con su supervisor si tienen preguntas sobre el reembolso.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "travel", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Business Travel", "title_es": "Viajes de Negocios", "body_en": "<p>Business travel must be approved in advance by the employee's supervisor. Employees are expected to book the most economical option that reasonably meets the business need and to use any Company-designated booking process or preferred vendors.</p><p>The Company reimburses reasonable and necessary travel expenses, including transportation, lodging, checked baggage, ground transportation, parking, tolls, business calls, and meals within Company limits. Personal entertainment, in-room movies, spouse or companion travel, traffic and parking fines, and upgrades not approved in advance are not reimbursable. Alcohol is reimbursable only where the Company has expressly approved it as part of a client meal.</p><p>Receipts are required for all expenses at or above the threshold set by {{HR_CONTACT}}. Expense reports must be submitted within thirty days of the completion of travel. Where an employee uses a personal vehicle for approved business travel, mileage is reimbursed at the current IRS standard rate; the employee must maintain valid insurance and a valid license.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Los viajes de negocios deben ser aprobados previamente por el supervisor del empleado. Se espera que los empleados reserven la opción más económica que satisfaga razonablemente la necesidad del negocio y que utilicen el proceso de reserva designado por la Compañía o los proveedores preferidos.</p><p>La Compañía reembolsa los gastos de viaje razonables y necesarios, incluidos transporte, alojamiento, equipaje documentado, transporte terrestre, estacionamiento, peajes, llamadas de negocios y comidas dentro de los límites de la Compañía. No son reembolsables el entretenimiento personal, las películas en la habitación, los viajes de cónyuge o acompañante, las multas de tránsito y estacionamiento, y las mejoras de categoría no aprobadas previamente. El alcohol es reembolsable únicamente cuando la Compañía lo haya aprobado expresamente como parte de una comida con un cliente.</p><p>Se exigen recibos para todos los gastos que alcancen o superen el umbral fijado por {{HR_CONTACT}}. Los informes de gastos deben presentarse dentro de los treinta días posteriores a la finalización del viaje. Cuando un empleado use un vehículo personal para un viaje de negocios aprobado, el kilometraje se reembolsa a la tarifa estándar vigente del IRS; el empleado debe mantener un seguro válido y una licencia vigente.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "attendance", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Attendance & Punctuality", "title_es": "Asistencia y Puntualidad", "body_en": "<p>Regular attendance and punctuality are essential. If you will be late or absent, notify your supervisor as early as possible in accordance with Company call-in procedures. Excessive absenteeism or tardiness, or failure to notify the Company, may result in discipline, up to and including termination. Absences protected by law will be handled in accordance with the applicable leave policy.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La asistencia regular y la puntualidad son esenciales. Si va a llegar tarde o a ausentarse, notifique a su supervisor lo antes posible de acuerdo con los procedimientos de aviso de la Compañía. El ausentismo o la impuntualidad excesivos, o no notificar a la Compañía, pueden dar lugar a medidas disciplinarias, hasta e incluyendo el despido. Las ausencias protegidas por la ley se manejarán de acuerdo con la política de licencia aplicable.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "weather", "group": "Section 2: Workplace & Compensation", "title_en": "Inclement Weather & Emergency Closures", "title_es": "Clima Severo y Cierres de Emergencia", "body_en": "<p>The Company remains open during normal business hours unless a closure is announced. A decision to close, delay opening, or release employees early is made by management and communicated by {{HR_CONTACT}} through the Company's designated notification method. Employees should not assume a closure based on school or government announcements.</p><p>When the Company closes for all or part of a scheduled workday, exempt employees are paid their full salary for that week. Non-exempt employees are paid for hours actually worked and may use available paid time off to cover the remainder, unless state law provides otherwise or reporting-time pay is required. Employees who are able to work remotely may be asked to do so.</p><p>No employee is expected to travel in conditions the employee reasonably believes to be unsafe. An employee who cannot safely report to work on a day the Company is open should notify a supervisor as early as possible and may use available paid time off. Employees designated as essential personnel will be notified in advance of that designation.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía permanece abierta durante el horario laboral normal salvo que se anuncie un cierre. La decisión de cerrar, retrasar la apertura o dejar salir a los empleados antes de tiempo la toma la gerencia y la comunica {{HR_CONTACT}} a través del método de notificación designado por la Compañía. Los empleados no deben suponer que hay un cierre basándose en anuncios escolares o gubernamentales.</p><p>Cuando la Compañía cierra durante todo o parte de un día laboral programado, los empleados exentos reciben su salario completo de esa semana. Los empleados no exentos reciben pago por las horas efectivamente trabajadas y pueden usar tiempo libre remunerado disponible para cubrir el resto, salvo que la ley estatal disponga lo contrario o se exija pago por presentarse a trabajar. A los empleados que puedan trabajar de forma remota se les puede pedir que lo hagan.</p><p>No se espera que ningún empleado viaje en condiciones que razonablemente considere inseguras. El empleado que no pueda presentarse a trabajar de forma segura un día en que la Compañía esté abierta debe notificar a un supervisor lo antes posible y puede usar tiempo libre remunerado disponible. Los empleados designados como personal esencial serán notificados de esa designación con anticipación.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "benefits_overview", "group": "Section 3: Benefits & Time Off", "title_en": "Benefits Overview", "title_es": "Resumen de Beneficios", "body_en": "<p>The Company offers a range of benefits to eligible employees. This handbook summarizes them in general terms only. The specific terms, eligibility, and conditions of each benefit plan are governed by the official plan documents and insurance contracts, which control in the event of any difference with this handbook. The Company may change, add, or discontinue benefits at any time consistent with applicable law and plan terms.</p>", "body_es": "<p>La Compañía ofrece una variedad de beneficios a los empleados elegibles. Este manual los resume solo en términos generales. Los términos, la elegibilidad y las condiciones específicas de cada plan de beneficios se rigen por los documentos oficiales del plan y los contratos de seguro, que prevalecen en caso de cualquier diferencia con este manual. La Compañía puede cambiar, agregar o discontinuar beneficios en cualquier momento de conformidad con la ley aplicable y los términos del plan.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "enroll_when", "group": "Section 3: Benefits & Time Off", "title_en": "When You Can Enroll", "title_es": "Cuándo Puede Inscribirse", "body_en": "<p>There are three times you can enroll in or change your benefits.</p><p><strong>When you are first eligible.</strong> New employees may enroll during the initial enrollment window described in your offer or benefits summary. If you do not enroll during that window, you must wait for open enrollment unless you have a qualifying life event.</p><p><strong>Open enrollment.</strong> Once a year the Company holds an open enrollment period. This is the one time you can add, drop or change coverage for any reason. Elections made during open enrollment take effect on the first day of the new plan year and generally cannot be changed until the following year.</p><p><strong>A qualifying life event.</strong> Certain life changes let you change coverage mid-year, see the next section. You generally have <strong>30 days</strong> from the event to make the change, and the Company may require documentation.</p><p>If you take no action during open enrollment, your current elections may carry forward or may default to no coverage, depending on the plan. Read the enrollment materials each year; do not assume.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Hay tres momentos en los que puede inscribirse o cambiar sus beneficios.</p><p><strong>Cuando es elegible por primera vez.</strong> Los empleados nuevos pueden inscribirse durante el período de inscripción inicial descrito en su oferta o resumen de beneficios. Si no se inscribe durante ese período, deberá esperar a la inscripción abierta, salvo que tenga un evento de vida calificado.</p><p><strong>Inscripción abierta.</strong> Una vez al año la Compañía realiza un período de inscripción abierta. Es el único momento en que puede agregar, cancelar o cambiar la cobertura por cualquier motivo. Las elecciones hechas durante la inscripción abierta entran en vigor el primer día del nuevo año del plan y por lo general no pueden cambiarse hasta el año siguiente.</p><p><strong>Un evento de vida calificado.</strong> Ciertos cambios de vida le permiten modificar la cobertura a mitad de año, consulte la siguiente sección. Generalmente dispone de <strong>30 días</strong> desde el evento para hacer el cambio, y la Compañía puede exigir documentación.</p><p>Si no toma ninguna acción durante la inscripción abierta, sus elecciones actuales pueden mantenerse o pasar a ninguna cobertura, según el plan. Lea los materiales de inscripción cada año; no lo dé por sentado.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "enroll_qle", "group": "Section 3: Benefits & Time Off", "title_en": "Qualifying Life Events", "title_es": "Eventos de Vida Calificados", "body_en": "<p>A qualifying life event lets you change your benefit elections outside of open enrollment. The change you make must be consistent with the event.</p><p>Common qualifying events include marriage, divorce or legal separation; the birth, adoption or placement for adoption of a child; the death of a spouse or dependent; a dependent gaining or losing eligibility, including a child reaching the plan's age limit; you or your spouse gaining or losing other coverage, including through a change in employment status or a reduction in hours; a change in residence that affects plan availability; and certain court orders or changes in Medicare or Medicaid eligibility.</p><p><strong>You have 30 days from the date of the event</strong> to notify {{HR_CONTACT}} and complete the change, 60 days for events involving Medicaid or CHIP eligibility. Miss the window and you wait until open enrollment. Documentation such as a marriage certificate, birth certificate or a letter showing loss of prior coverage is generally required.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Un evento de vida calificado le permite cambiar sus elecciones de beneficios fuera de la inscripción abierta. El cambio que realice debe ser congruente con el evento.</p><p>Los eventos calificados comunes incluyen matrimonio, divorcio o separación legal; el nacimiento, la adopción o la colocación para adopción de un hijo; el fallecimiento de un cónyuge o dependiente; que un dependiente adquiera o pierda la elegibilidad, incluido un hijo que alcance el límite de edad del plan; que usted o su cónyuge obtenga o pierda otra cobertura, incluso por un cambio en la situación laboral o una reducción de horas; un cambio de residencia que afecte la disponibilidad del plan; y ciertas órdenes judiciales o cambios en la elegibilidad para Medicare o Medicaid.</p><p><strong>Dispone de 30 días a partir de la fecha del evento</strong> para notificar a {{HR_CONTACT}} y completar el cambio, 60 días para eventos relacionados con la elegibilidad para Medicaid o CHIP. Si pierde el plazo, deberá esperar a la inscripción abierta. Por lo general se exige documentación, como un acta de matrimonio, un acta de nacimiento o una carta que acredite la pérdida de la cobertura anterior.</p>", "optional": true, "state": false}, {"id": "health", "group": "Section 3: Benefits & Time Off", "title_en": "Health & Insurance Benefits", "title_es": "Beneficios de Salud y Seguro", "body_en": "<p>Eligible employees may participate in the Company's health and related insurance benefits, subject to the terms of the applicable plans. Human Resources can provide summary plan descriptions and enrollment information. Continuation of coverage after certain qualifying events may be available under COBRA or applicable state continuation law.</p>", "body_es": "<p>Los empleados elegibles pueden participar en los beneficios de salud y seguros relacionados de la Compañía, sujetos a los términos de los planes aplicables. Recursos Humanos puede proporcionar descripciones resumidas del plan e información de inscripción. La continuación de la cobertura después de ciertos eventos calificados puede estar disponible bajo COBRA o la ley estatal de continuación aplicable.</p>", "optional": false, "state": false}, {"id": "enroll_terms", "group": "Section 3: Benefits & Time Off", "title_en": "Understanding Your Benefits: Plain English", "title_es": "Entender Sus Beneficios: En Palabras Sencillas", "body_en": "<p>Benefits paperwork is full of terms that are rarely explained. Here is what they actually mean.</p><p><strong>Premium</strong>, what the coverage costs each pay period, whether or not you use it. Your share is deducted from your paycheck.</p><p><strong>Deductible</strong>, what you pay out of pocket each plan year before the plan starts paying its share. A $2,000 deductible means the first $2,000 of covered care is yours.</p><p><strong>Copay</strong>, a flat amount for a specific service, such as $30 to see a doctor. Copays often apply before you meet the deductible.</p><p><strong>Coinsurance</strong> (after the deductible, the percentage you keep paying. “80/20” means the plan pays 80% and you pay 20%.</p><p><strong>Out-of-pocket maximum</strong>) the most you can pay in a plan year. Once you reach it, the plan pays 100% of covered in-network care. This is the number that protects you from a catastrophe.</p><p><strong>In-network</strong>, providers who agreed to discounted rates. Going out of network costs dramatically more, and sometimes is not covered at all. Check before you book.</p><p><strong>HSA and FSA</strong>, accounts that let you pay medical costs with pre-tax dollars. An HSA requires a high-deductible plan, the money is yours permanently and it rolls over. An FSA does not require a specific plan, but is largely use-it-or-lose-it within the plan year.</p>", "body_es": "<p>El papeleo de beneficios está lleno de términos que rara vez se explican. Esto es lo que significan.</p><p><strong>Prima</strong>, lo que cuesta la cobertura en cada período de pago, la use o no. Su parte se descuenta de su check.</p><p><strong>Deducible</strong>, lo que paga de su bolsillo cada año del plan antes de que el plan empiece a pagar su parte.
